outline.chapter_title: From Foundation Models to Orthogonal Butterfly Finetuning
outline.description: Introduce the motivation for parameter-efficient finetuning of large foundation models, limitations of existing approaches, and the high-level idea behind Orthogonal Butterfly (BOFT). Summarize the paper’s contributions and the roadmap of the textbook.
subtopics: Why full finetuning is impractical for modern foundation models
PEFT goals: strong transfer, small parameter budgets, no latency
Three PEFT families: model finetuning, adapters, prompts
Why orthogonality as a finetuning prior
Limitations of block-diagonal OFT and the need for density
High-level idea of composing dense orthogonal transforms from sparse ones
Butterfly insight from fast Fourier transforms
Contributions and scope of BOFT

outline.description: Review the linear algebra and optimization tools needed to understand OFT and BOFT, focusing on orthogonal matrices, skew-symmetric parameterizations, and spectral properties relevant to stable finetuning.
subtopics: Orthogonal matrices: properties, stability, and angle preservation
Skew-symmetric matrices and the Cayley transform
Preserving neuron pairwise angles and its significance
Spectral norm and singular value decomposition
Block matrices, permutations, and sparsity patterns
Parameter counting: dense vs sparse vs low rank
Computational trade-offs: time versus parameter storage

outline.description: Present the OFT framework, how it preserves pretrained structure, and why the original block-diagonal parameterization limits expressivity and induces undesirable inductive biases.
subtopics: OFT formulation: reparameterize W as R W0
Neuron geometry preservation and zero initialization
Maintaining orthogonality during training via Cayley

Inductive biases from block partitioning by indices

Empirical stability of OFT and its parameter overhead

outline.chapter_title: An Information Transmission View of Matrix Factorization
outline.description: Recast constructing dense orthogonal matrices as information transmission on layered graphs, clarifying how sparse factors compose dense connectivity and guiding the search for efficient structures.
subtopics: Mapping matrix products to layered grid graphs
Edges as nonzeros: when information can flow
Dense connectivity requirement across layers

Design desiderata from the transmission viewpoint

outline.description: Explain butterfly graphs from the Cooley-Tukey FFT algorithm and their efficiency in globally mixing information with only O(d log d) nonzeros.
subtopics: Cooley-Tukey FFT and recursive decomposition
Butterfly graphs: topology and mixing behavior

Why butterfly achieves global mixing efficiently

Implications for parameter-efficient dense transforms

outline.description: Detail the BOFT framework: how to build an orthogonal finetuning matrix as a product of orthogonal butterfly components, its relation to OFT, and parameter efficiency.

outline.description: Provide implementation guidance: initialization, maintaining orthogonality, regularization via multiplicative dropout, and systems considerations for integration with modern architectures.
